TYPE workout

Pre-illness maxes: bench 100kg, squat 140kg, deadlift 170kg.

After 3 weeks off plus illness-related fatigue and 4kg weight loss, expect roughly 10–15% strength reduction on return. Week 1 is programmed at RPE 5 — that is a very conservative reintroduction, leaving significant room in the tank. The working numbers should sit around 60–65% of pre-illness 1RM.

Estimated working loads for Week 1:

Bench Press — 3x10 RPE 5
Pre-illness 1RM 100kg. 60–65% = 60–65kg. Start at 60kg. This will feel easy. That is correct.

Squat — 3x8 RPE 5
Pre-illness 1RM 140kg. 60–65% = 84–91kg. Start at 80kg. The 4kg bodyweight loss and post-illness fatigue make the lower end appropriate here. Squat is the most systemically demanding of the three.

Deadlift — 3x6 RPE 5
Pre-illness 1RM 170kg. 60–65% = 102–110kg. Start at 100kg. Fewer reps than squat because deadlift fatigue accumulates quickly and CNS cost is high when returning from a layoff.

Key coaching notes for Week 1:

These numbers should feel almost embarrassingly light. That is the point. The goal this week is not stimulus — it is movement quality, connective tissue reloading, and nervous system reactivation. If he hits RPE 7 or above on any of these sets, the load is too high and should be reduced immediately. Fatigue from illness is not always linear — he may feel fine on Monday and significantly worse by Friday. Build in permission to drop load on Friday if needed. Do not let him chase his old numbers before Week 3.

The programme already uses cycling and rowing as warmup modalities. Adding structured running reconditioning on top of the 3-day lifting block requires care — post-illness fatigue plus 4kg weight loss means respiratory and cardiovascular capacity will lag behind muscular capacity. Jumping straight back to 10k is contraindicated in Week 1.

Structure: running sessions sit on Tuesday and Thursday, the natural gaps between lifting days. Saturday is optional easy effort. Total weekly running volume builds across the 3 weeks toward 10k.
